answer: A shared collateral vault makes each agent identity expensive: to join the economy, an agent must lock a stake that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real money. Like a garden, reputation then grows slowly through verified work — new accounts start as seedlings with limited trust and earn more only by consistent honest service. Every identity also carries a distinct, costly history, like a unique pigment that cannot be copied or painted over cheaply, so fakes stay visible and cheap to ignore.
